options.text: Reverse automatically because it was the original plan
Pass through D2’s marker without checking
Reassess a hold or another outlet

before.explanation: A closed second option means another read is needed; holding may be useful if possession can be protected.

after.prompt: YOU want to advance as far toward centre ice as these outlets allow, without sending the puck farther toward the side boards. Which pass would you assess?

options.text: Pass to W
Pass to C
Pass to D2

after.explanation: C gives more progress toward centre ice than D2 while receiving nearer the middle than the puck is now. W offers more forward distance but is wider. Check the passing line before release: this identifies an option to assess, not a guaranteed safe pass. A reverse to D2 or a wider pass to W may suit a different aim or a changed picture.

D2 x=-24 gives zero advance from rendered puck, with |y|6.7 to6. A reverse is plausible but less advance than C.

The pass from D1 to C

C is an option for D1 to assess while YOU continue offering support; YOU do not have to receive the next pass. This still frame does not prove either pass will succeed. The line to YOU may become useful as the players move.

before.prompt: Gold 1 moves directly onto your new lane. What might you do?

options.text: Rush beside F1 and remove the deeper option

after.prompt: Gold 1 is near the pass from D1 to YOU. To begin offering deeper middle support, which direction changes your passing angle more than skating straight toward D1?

options.text: Take a few strides toward F1
Take a few strides toward D1
Take a few strides toward the centre faceoff dot

after.explanation: Moving toward the centre faceoff dot takes YOU back and inward while changing the angle of the line from D1 to YOU. Moving straight toward D1 mainly shortens that same line near Gold 1; moving toward F1 takes YOU farther up ice and wider. Gold 1 is nearby, can move and may still reach the new line. Check again; a changed angle does not establish an open or completed pass.

optionReasons.reason: F1 is farther up ice and wider; high support is plausible but not deeper-middle.
Directly toward D1 preserves actor-centre line bearing. May shorten support but not substantially change the alignment.
Centre dot(0,0) is back and inward from YOU(2,6); direction changes D1-to-YOU bearing. No clearance guarantee.
